Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.sqlite

Class SQLiteConnector

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.sqlite.SQLiteConnector
All Implemented Interfaces:
Connector
public final class SQLiteConnector extends Object implements Connector
The Connector for SQLite, driver name sqlite.

The database setting is a file path or :memory:. A url setting, when present, replaces both and is used as given. The foreign_keys option turns foreign key enforcement on or off for every connection; it is on unless set to false, as in Laravel.

An in-memory database (:memory:, or a url of jdbc:sqlite::memory:, jdbc:sqlite:file::memory: or any URL with mode=memory) is private to one JDBC connection in SQLite. The connector therefore opens one connection, keeps it for the life of the Diwan connection and lends it to one session at a time; a second session waits until the first ends, up to the busy_timeout option in milliseconds (default 30000), then fails with an SQLException. The data lives until close(Connection) runs, that is, until the manager purges or closes the connection. A session that needs the database while another session of the same thread holds it, such as a seeder that queries inside its own transaction, must use the transaction's connection.

The transaction_mode option, deferred, immediate or exclusive in any case, sets how a transaction begins and is passed to the driver as transaction_mode=<UPPER> unless the URL already names it; unset leaves the driver's default, deferred. A deferred transaction that reads and then writes can fail with a busy error when another writer got in between; immediate takes the write lock at the start and makes writers queue. The busy_timeout option, when set, is also passed to every URL the connector builds, file or in-memory, as busy_timeout=<milliseconds> unless the URL names it, so a writer waits that long for the lock; unset leaves the driver's own wait. The lock_wait option, a duration such as 5s or 500ms, is another spelling of busy_timeout; when both are set they must name the same number of milliseconds.

When the application supplies a DataSource, it is used as is: no URL is built, no option, including transaction_mode and busy_timeout, is applied and no connection is held back. A connection it hands out in manual-commit mode still commits through the driver's commit(), which begins a new transaction in immediate mode.

Instances are safe to share across threads and across connection names.

    • connect

      public Connection connect(ConnectionConfig config, DataSource dataSource)
      Builds a connection for a config.

      When the connector needs a resource that outlives the call, such as the anchor connection that keeps an in-memory database alive, it keeps the resource and releases it in Connector.close(Connection).

      Specified by:
      connect in interface Connector
      Parameters:
      config - the connection config, never null
      dataSource - the data source the user registered for this connection, or null when the connector must build its own from the config
      Returns:
      the connection, never null
      Throws:
      DatabaseConfigException - if neither url nor database is set, if foreign_keys is not a boolean, if transaction_mode is not deferred, immediate or exclusive, if busy_timeout is not a number of milliseconds, zero or more, if lock_wait is not a positive duration, or if both are set and differ
      IllegalStateException - if the in-memory database cannot be opened

    • close

      public void close(Connection connection)
      Releases what Connector.connect(org.aristonis.diwan.database.manager.ConnectionConfig, javax.sql.DataSource) kept for a connection, once the manager drops it.

      The manager calls this on purge, disconnect and close, before it closes a data source the user registered. The default does nothing.

      Closes the connection of an in-memory database, which drops the database. Does nothing for a connection without one.

      Specified by:
      close in interface Connector
      Parameters:
      connection - the connection Connector.connect(org.aristonis.diwan.database.manager.ConnectionConfig, javax.sql.DataSource) returned, never null
